articles.title: “COME, SEE THE PLACE WHERE THE LORD LAY”
articles.author: Dr. S. D. K. Roberts

paragraphs.text: The angel, dear brethren, knew just why the women had come to the sepulchre, and the Holy Spirit knows why each one has come here today. There were those around at that time who were against Christ, but we have come as those who have affection for Him. We have come to pay respect to our dearly-loved departed brother, and this is right. We have not come to eulogise him. There is no need for this, for we knew him and, as already mentioned in prayer, know his fidelity to the truth and his affection for Christ. How his face would light up whenever the name of the Lord Jesus was mentioned!

We have come here, too, because of our affection for the sorrowing ones. We are glad to show our affection for our beloved sister and the sisters of our brother. However, the time will come when there will be no need of sympathy, for every tear will be wiped away; no grief, no sorrow any more! Meanwhile the love and sympathy of Christ, expressed through His own, will be a great comfort to the sorrowing ones.

But there is another reason why we are here, and I am sure that it is the most important; it is that we may receive some fresh impression of Christ. When other reasons for our being here will have passed for ever, the impressions we receive by the

Spirit of the Lord Jesus today will last for eternity—never to be erased! There are many impressions of Christ that could be received at a time like this, of His life here, His death, His resurrection, His ascension and glorification, but the present occasion would serve to give us some impression—for eternity—of Christ as He lay in death.
You will notice that the angel changes from the name of Jesus to ‘the Lord’—“Fear not ye, for I know that ye seek Jesus the crucified one. He is not here, for he is risen, as he said.

Come, see the place where the Lord lay”. What a spectacle—to see the place where the Lord lay! the One who later says, “All power has been given me in heaven and upon earth”, Matthew 28: 18. As we view that place in a fresh way today we shall find that any pride in us will recede, finally to disappear, with all self-esteem, when, as Mr. Darby says in his hymn—
‘All thought of self is now for ever o’er’—every heart finding in Christ its unmingled object.
Think of eternity with no thought of self, but Christ filling the vision.

The Lord has allowed many deaths and burials amongst us lately, and there is something for us to learn as to the burial of Christ. He went into the grave on our account, having voluntarily given up His life in order to remove for us death as a penalty, having already exhausted God’s just judgment on sin. In His vicarious death and burial He has also removed from God’s eye the order of man that incurred the penalty of death. How wonderful! The tomb is now empty!
I think the most testing time for the sorrowing ones is the moment of burial. I would like to

commend to our dear sister and all the sorrowing ones that, as our beloved brother is actually buried, and the break for ever of the natural tie is realised, the vision may fill their souls of the place where the Lord lay. He is not there now! He has been into the grave, into death itself, but the tomb hewn in the rock, and the stone, could not hold Him there; “He is risen, as he said”. The stone was not rolled away by the angel to let Him out, but to show the women that He was not there. He is now not only risen, but ascended and glorified, and the link that our much-loved brother had with Him while here can never be broken, no, not for a moment.
He is now with Christ, in the communion of love, and soon will have his body of glory.

articles.title: “THE FATHER HIMSELF HAS AFFECTION FOR YOU”
articles.author: C. R. Byng

paragraphs.text: The Spirit of God would be affecting us as to the love of Christ that led Him to go into the tomb, and as to the love of the Father Himself. The Spirit would make this freshly real to those of the family, and to all of us, “The Father himself has affection for you”.

We are feeling the sorrow at this time as having some impression of the divine love that has entered into it. But the very consciousness that our beloved brother has fallen asleep through Jesus immediately connects our hearts and affections with Jesus where He is. How real it is that our brother is “absent from the body”, but he is “present with

the Lord”, 2 Corinthians 5: 8. This is the assurance that steadies our hearts at a time like this, that our brother is “present with the Lord”. What fulness of joy is his; as Paul says, it is “very much better”, Philippians 1: 24.

We are here as those who grieve, but we have hope as those who are looking forward to the resurrection. Our hearts would be affected by the love of Jesus that took Him through the sufferings of death into death itself. What death meant to Jesus! Death is swallowed up in victory now as a result of the mighty work of the Lord Jesus. Entering into every detail of His life there is what is infinite in glory. His sufferings, His death, His burial, and His resurrection have a glory that is infinite and inscrutable. And yet the love that found expression through the very midst of those sufferings is intended to draw our hearts, beloved brethren, to Jesus in the realm where He is. The Spirit of God would bind our hearts to the Lord Jesus where He is as we think of the love that led Him to go such a way that we might, as we think of death, think of it as the way into the glory where Jesus is.

The power of this present occasion is to result in our having a deeper impression of our links with the Father Himself. “The Father himself has affection for you, because ye have had affection for me”. It was affection for Jesus that held our brother in the steadiness of the pathway that was his. He knew what it was to share in assembly sorrows as well as assembly joys. He had family sorrows as well as family joys. He had pressure in his body. But, through it all, it was affection for Jesus that held him steady and gave him the fatherly influence amongst the brethren which will remain as an impression with us of the character of

the work of God in him. What an influence for good he has been as he filled out what he was given to do in a way which betokened his nearness to Jesus. The spirit of Christ that was in our brother is intended to be an influence amongst us still so that we may enjoy eternal life conditions as having some abiding impression of the way that the Spirit strengthened him.

Then, too, I think he had an abiding sense of the Father’s love. It is the Father’s love that would peculiarly lay hold of the heart of our beloved sister, and of the sisters of our brother, and of all the family—some are here, and we are glad to see them; some are not here, but the Spirit of God can give them an impression of the Father’s affection. There is to be something which steadies us and binds us to the Lord Jesus in the realm where He is, as we remain here with a sense of the Father’s love. So we desire, with help from on high, to be here as those who are pleasing to God, moving in such a way that we too, each of us, may be an influence for good amongst the beloved brethren, and amongst men generally, until the day when we see Jesus face to face.

The Lord Jesus has gone out of this world. He was leaving this world, as He says, but He is coming again very soon. In the meantime, in the very short while that remains, as our hearts are strengthened by the Father’s love, we are to be held here as those that are waiting for our Lord until He comes to take us away to be in the presence of God for ever. May we be encouraged, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: MIGHTY MEN
articles.author: E. C. Burr
articles.meeting: Words at the burial of Mr, J. Thomson
footer: (The meeting was held at West Norwood, London).

paragraphs.text: What has been said, both in prayer and by our beloved brother who has just spoken, as to the history of our beloved brother whose body is before us now, draws me to this scripture. His history is well known to us, a history beginning, according to God, with his faith in our Lord Jesus Christ as Saviour. As the apostle Paul says, “Christ died for our sins … and … he was buried … and … he was raised the third day, according to the scriptures”, 1 Corinthians 15: 3, 4. Christ thus becoming the object of faith to men, and to our beloved brother, becomes the means of the eternal standing and security to which reference has already been made.

I suppose it might be more current with us all, when we have believed in the Lord Jesus and found how much we owe to Him, that we are surprised, as we should be surprised, that in the world He is rejected. The Man that the world needs and that every man and woman, young person, and even child, needs, and who is available to them—being the means of such blessing to souls—yet He is rejected. It is a position that we all have to understand as believers, that Christ is rejected.
This point in the history of David embraces a time when he was rejected. (In the first book of Chronicles the mighty men are put at the beginning

of the history; in Samuel they are put towards the close). But how this list of the mighty men begins is, “These are the names of the mighty men whom David had”. And that is related to the affection for Christ of which our beloved brother has just spoken, attachment to Him, so that it can be said of one and another that ‘He has them’; ‘the mighty men whom David had’.

They are not just men enlisted in the army, but they are men that David had. And the affection which our beloved brother had for the Lord Jesus would put him among the men that Christ had; men that, from another point of view, the Father gave to Him out of the world, but men that He had; “They were thine, and thou gavest them me”, John 17: 6. And there is a long series of men at the end of the chapter of whom nothing in particular is said, save that they were among the men that David had.

But, as the list begins, we have certain individuals. We have a man in verse 8 about whom I did not read, and then we have these other two men, and it is these two men that draw me to the recollection of our beloved brother. I refer first to Shammah because it says of him that he stood in the plot of lentils. There was “a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people had fled

… and he stood in the midst of the plot and delivered it”. Beloved, those who know our brother’s history will have no difficulty in identifying him with this kind of thing, the plot of ground perhaps speaking of a brother’s own locality. Our beloved brother has stood for the truth in his own locality, stood—we might say stood and stood—stood for the truth in his own place; stood in the area where the food was; stood to defend it.
I do not apply now in any detail what the Philistines might be, save that they are an element

which is opposed to the progress of the people of God, both as to enjoyment and as to the truth. But our beloved brother is identifiable as one who has stood in the plot of lentils in his day. And God gave a great deliverance. Issues arise in localities and they have to be resolved in localities. But, through their being resolved in the localities where they are, God may give a great deliverance to His people. May we thus have confidence in local assemblies.

We are all tested, both brothers and sisters, as to whether we have this kind of fibre; whether we are content to let someone else defend the truth or whether we ourselves will stand in the plot and defend it ourselves. For, as our beloved brother has said, not only will the savour of our beloved brother’s life among us remain, but his example will remain.

None of these first three men, I think, is heard of anywhere else save in the lists of the mighty men. It would be a great thing to find that one was inscribed in the divine record as one who had stood in a plot of lentils in his day and that, through him, God had given a great deliverance. Beloved, it tests us as to what we are in our own place; the place where we belong; the place where every issue that arises will be resolved. This plot of lentils was the place where the issue had to be taken up, and it was taken up. As I say, our knowledge of our beloved brother’s history gives us no difficulty in identifying him with this kind of thing. Are we prepared to be this kind of man?—this kind of woman, for that matter? Are we prepared to be this kind of person? because a meeting like this bears not only on the comfort of the saints, but on the continuance of the testimony.

I refer to the second man last. There was Joseb-Bassebeth in verse 8, and then there was Eleazar, and then there was Shammah. I refer to Eleazar because, in a sense, his experience is one that, for us, comes after the experience of Shammah, that is “He arose and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary”. Beloved, I do not think this is the weariness that gives up or that thinks that conflict has gone on long enough and therefore one will retire from it. I think this is the weariness of “I am already being poured out” (2 Timothy 4: 6), that is to say, as far as this man was concerned, there was nothing more that he could do; but, even when he was weary, his hand still clave to the sword. We can see that, too, in our beloved brother, on account of whose death we are here today, that he fought until he was weary and his hand clave to the sword—even then. What an example for us!

I trust none of us have things patterned out so that we have in our minds a time when we will retire from testimonial energy and from conflict. This man went on until he was weary. I think it corresponds to “I have fought the good fight”, 2 Timothy 4: 7, A.V. I think this man corresponds to “I am already being poured out”. And again, through Eleazar, God gave a great deliverance. It shows what God can accomplish through people who are determined to go on to the end in the conflicts of the testimony.

Then it says, “the people returned after him only to spoil”. That is to say that what he stood for, and the way he stood, accomplished great things, accomplished deliverance, and out of it came vast profit for all the people, they “returned after him only to spoil”. No one else, after him, had to do anything. We shall never reach that kind of

situation where we can retire because one man has accomplished everything, save for what Christ as one Man has accomplished; but this man stood and he fought till he was weary and, after him, they returned only to spoil.

It is like Paul, as I say again, “I am already being poured out”, and after Paul the rest of us, I suppose, have returned only to spoil. We have found vast gain through what he did in his application of his life to the testimony, ultimately coming, as he says, to having finished his course. He went on in the combat until he was weary and God gave a great deliverance; for the rest of the people there was only spoil.

Well, beloved, may we be concerned not only to apply ourselves, to commit ourselves to continuing to apply ourselves, but may we also enjoy the spoil which comes from consistent adherence to the truth of God.

For those who have confessed Him, I would suggest the next stage in our soul history is that the Lord would have us brought to a definite committal to Him. We have to lament the indecision of so many young believers. If you have one foot in the world, you will soon find both feet there. It is vain to try to make the best of both worlds; you will not make the best of either. The Lord has moved the hearts of His people for you that you might be brought to a point in your soul history, that out of true affection for Him, you may be definitely committed to Him and to His beloved people. I love that man who was lame who sat at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful (Acts 3: 1–10). The moment he was healed he took his stand alongside the followers of Jesus. Splendid! Have you done that? Have you been converted a long time and yet have never thrown your lot in with them?

Think of what you are missing! What did he get? He walked and leaped and praised God, and he entered with them into the temple. That is where the Lord wants you. He would take possession of your affections; He would secure possession of you by causing you wholeheartedly to respond to Him; He would lead you to be found with them who find their joy in the presence of God, in the service of God, and in the worship of God.

In the goodness of our God, some of us have been tasting together the joys that belong to those who are His beloved children. We have been engaged during the past two days with things that are new, things that are of God, things that are divine, and things that are glorious and wonderful, and our hearts have been stirred to their depths as we have shared those joys.

Our hearts have gone up to the Lord for you, for He wants you to share them too. Many of those engaged in this happy occupation are old and grey-headed, and, if the Lord tarry, many, of them may soon be taken home. But we are assured that the Lord is getting ready a generation to follow. He is making an appeal for young men and young women with hearts devoted to Him, as divinely moved by the love of Christ, to be ready to step forward and say, ‘Lord, I desire to follow Thee’. Such will be ready to stand with those who love Him, ready to go into the temple with them, to engage in the holy worship of God with them, to sing with them, to praise with them, and ready to come out with them and stand with them as they suffer reproach, shame, and dishonour for His name.

Are you ready for that? Have you ever weighed it over in the presence of the Lord Jesus that He gave His life for you, that He is entitled to have you, spirit, soul and body, for His pleasure, His joy, His service and for the worship of His name? Are you ready to say, ‘Lord, Thou art worthy; I would desire to be devoted to Thee’? What a moment it is in our soul history when the love of Christ in all its magnificent power so controls the heart that we are ready to commit ourselves in true devotedness and affection to Jesus. Let me put it in scriptural language, as it is put so beautifully by the apostle, “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the compassions of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your intelligent service” ... He wants you, not a part of you, not for an hour or two a week; He wants you, your heart, mind and body, your interests, and your affections. He wants you in every position, so that your hands, as clean, may be used to express your identification with His beloved saints who are here, in true affection, remembering Him. What would not the Lord do with a body presented to Him as a living sacrifice? Dear young friends, if only you realised the tremendous possibilities of your life if held by Christ in the power of His love, you would never hold it for one moment in your own keeping. You would surrender it to Him, to be held by Him and for Him until He shall come, and you would enter, at that moment of committal, upon the sweetest, and purest, and happiest life it is possible to live on earth.

The Lord appeals to you, that you might not only be converted, not only confessing His blessed name, but that you might commit yourself entirely to Him. Can you trust Him with yourself? You have trusted Him concerning your soul’s eternal welfare. Cannot you trust your body to Him? Cannot you trust your lips, your hands, your mind, your life, your joys to Him? Will not the blessed Son of God, do better for you than you can do for yourself? Can He not secure for you a present, and eternal joy, and blessing that the world knows nothing of and can never give? How great is the appeal of the love of Jesus! What are the words of it?

“This do in remembrance of me”. I believe many a young believer’s life is a failure because he is not wholeheartedly committed. Many are content to come and be spectators, content with merely attending the meetings. What is that to the heart of Christ? He is waiting for your love. He has loved you unto death, and He loves you still with such a love—a present living love—that He wants you in possession, that He may fill you and use you for His glory, to make you profoundly happy in a path of wholeheartedness for Him.

I thank God I speak to many who have confessed His blessed name, and are already committed to Him and to His beloved people, who have tasted the joy of the remembrance of Himself in partaking of His Supper. They have in true devotedness stood with those who have entered into the temple and praised and blessed God, and have stood shoulder to shoulder with the saints as they have had to suffer reproach for His name, and to such I would desire to add a further thought. The Lord would give you a definite commission in relation to His interests here.
The scripture we read together (Acts 26: 13–18) was about Saul of Tarsus. I am not referring to

him now as an apostle, but as he himself speaks, “But for this reason mercy was shown me, that in me, the first, Jesus Christ might display the whole long-suffering, for a delineation of those about to believe on him”, 1 Timothy 1: 16. In that sense, I refer to the way in which the Lord commissioned him to be here as His servant for His pleasure … May I say a word to the dear young men? Have you received your commission? Have you waited upon the Lord for the definite word from Him as to what He would have you do, and where He would have you, relative to His interests here on earth? Have you received from Himself direct a consciousness, a living touch that has given you to realise that you are His servant, one ready to do His bidding? Have you heard Him say, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?”, Isaiah 6: 8. And have you said, in true affection for Him, “Here am I; send me”? Such are the men that the Lord will use today in His service and in His interests. Such are the brothers or sisters that the Lord will make fruitful for His glory and pleasure. Let me again ask in all affection, ‘Have you received your commission from the Lord in glory?’. It says that He left His house and gave “to each one his work”, Mark 13: 34. Have you received your work—

your life work? Face this question in the presence of your Lord. What is your life work? You have interests; you may have a well-developed, a well-educated mind; you may have a great sphere of life opening up before you, but what is your life work? What are you living for? Is wealth the object, or is it Christ? We are not commissioned to serve ourselves and to acquire the maximum of wealth that our efforts can secure; we are commissioned to do His bidding as His servants—His trusty servants—ready to stand in His power against His foes in His name, and for His sake.

The Lord is calling young men and young women that He might commission them in His service, for His glory; that He might fill up the ranks of those that are passing away, so that they might take their stand alongside those who are standing for Him.
From an address at Croydon in June 1926, printed in J.T. O.S. Vol. 82, p.
Whatsoever things are true,
These produce a glorious hue
On mind and heart, as thus we meet
And always with the truth to greet.
Honest things are food for thought,
These are treasures that are sought
‘Mid corruption, falsehood, sin,
Honesty shines bright therein.
Whatsoever things are just,
Virtues these that we can trust,
Justice marks our every deed
If right thoughts our minds do feed.
Pure in thought, Oh may we know
More of its transparent glow
Precious gem of priceless worth,
Purity of thought, set forth.
Lovely thoughts may fill our mind,
These will not be hard to find
If replenished be our store
Daily, hourly adding more.
Then there are the things we hear,
Good report from far and near.
Oh how wide becomes our range
As we happy thoughts exchange.
Other gracious thoughts are there,
Virtues rich that we may share;
Think on these things and thus know
Joys which earth can ne’er bestow.
All these precious features spring,
From the secret source within,
Known to those who love the Lord,
And believe His faithful word.
As God’s people meet and part,
May His love so fill each heart
That we may His features trace
‘Mongst His own through wondrous grace.
Help us, Lord, our thoughts to train,
Thus to reap eternal gain,
Blessedness e’en now to know
In our walk and ways below.

We were affected in the reading today by the Lord’s words in Luke 22: 69, as He stood before the council of the elders, chief priests and scribes—“But henceforth shall the Son of man be sitting on the right hand of the power of God”. The Epistle to the Hebrews engages our thoughts with the present position of Christ; indeed, we are to be constantly occupied with it. In Exodus 17, during the fight with Amalek, while Joshua and Israel were engaged in the conflict Moses was on the top of the hill engaged in intercession and support. Similarly, we are left here below, but yet, moment by moment, are to be aware of Christ’s position exalted at the right hand of God, in the place of supremacy and power—power that is exercised in relation to us and is in our favour—indeed is in favour of all men. Jesus is not sitting there in judgment, but in glory and blessing, and is available to all men. Our second scripture shows us the greatness of the Person who is in that position in the heavens, who is our High Priest, and the third presents to us that same Person set down at the right hand of the throne of God to be our object and the source of encouragement and power as we run the race here.

How often we return to the opening of Hebrews 1, one of the grandest utterances in the whole of Scripture. I would touch on the end of verse 3, “who … having made by himself the purification of sins, set himself down on the right hand of the greatness on high”. This epistle was written for the benefit of Jewish believers and, for their help, it dwells on the offerings and the priesthood in the Old Testament types. It shows the contrast between those priests of old who were constantly offering sacrifices, and what we come to in Christ. On any given day a priest would be constantly offering sacrifices for various sins. When one day’s service was completed he knew that he must return the next day to resume his service, a service that must go on throughout his life. And when he reached the age of final retirement others would carry on that same repeated order of sacrifices. Hebrews shows, then, the contrast between that order of priesthood and Christ’s, throwing into glorious relief the uniqueness of Christ’s “Having made by himself the purification of sins”. That statement sums up His great work, involving His atoning sufferings, His death, the shedding of His blood. Thus did He make the purification of sins. The work also involved His burial and resurrection, and then He set Himself down on the right hand of the greatness on high. Never again shall there be a sin-offering! There has been one sacrifice for sins (Hebrews 10: 12). We need to contemplate the grandeur, the glory, the finality of His work in every aspect of it.

Christ was contemplated by us earlier as we viewed Him drawing nearer and nearer to the time when He would be the sin bearer and would be forsaken, when His soul would be made an offering for sin, and when the wrath of God would come upon Him, our Substitute. We were impressed by what Jesus suffered so patiently and meekly from the hands of men. What those sufferings meant to the spirit of Jesus—to be mocked and beaten, to be rejected by the leaders of His own people, for He came to His own and His own received Him not. What all that meant to His holy and infinitely keen sensibilities!—but, far beyond even that in its awfulness, to be forsaken by His God! What sin was to Him, yet He was made that very thing—“Him who knew not sin he has made sin for us, that we might become God’s righteousness in him”, 2 Corinthians 5: 21.

Jesus was prepared to go on steadfastly in devotion to God and in love to men. The believer in Jesus can say with Paul, “The Son of God, who has loved me and given himself for me”, Galatians 2: 20. Think of the love, the sacrifice, the sufferings, that entered into it!—and every believer can say, ‘It was for me’, and love and praise Him for it.
Then we can contemplate His magnificent action when, having accomplished redemption, He

“set himself down on the right hand of the greatness on high”. He entered into the very presence of God, that action demonstrating the glory of a finished work. The same Person who shortly before had been made sin now sets Himself down there. Every trace of sin has been removed; everything that had been required of Him has been done and completed in such a way that His is the glory of it. How worthy of that place on high He is—His alone the right to take it!

Now He is the great Administrator of blessing and is set forth by God “a mercy-seat, through faith in his blood”, Romans 3: 25. Divine power is operating on the basis of the work which Christ has done for God. He is undoing the works of the devil, operating throughout the world in the glad tidings to liberate men from sin, extricating them from its power and condemnation and securing them for God.

In Hebrews 8 we find that this same Person is our High Priest. The previous chapter tells us that He is “priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedec” (Hebrews 8: 17). His is an unchangeable priesthood, never to be transmitted to another. So here we have a precious summary; not only is Christ High Priest, but ‘ we have such a one high priest’. Jesus was not a priest on earth, though, of course, He ever acted in a priestly way; but in heaven He is now High Priest—what a Priest He is!—and in what a place of power—“sat down on the right hand of the throne of the greatness in the heavens”. It is the place of supremacy and exaltation. And it is for us— we have such a One. Old Testament saints might well boast of such a one as Aaron and the glory of his office; our boast is that we have such a One as our High Priest in the solitary greatness of His Person and of His place there. The law constituted men high priests who had infirmity, but our High Priest is a Son perfected for ever (Hebrews 7: 28).

How comforting this is! Whatever our experiences, our need, or our frailty, the glory of this Person, and His position, never change—He is there for us, sustaining all. We are carried upon His shoulders and on His breast. He is “minister of the holy places”. His first concern is that all shall be maintained for God. The holy places of old included the holy place and the holy of holies. He is there to sustain us so that we can answer to what the holy places suggest.

In the holy place there were the pure table and the shewbread—the saints before God in Christ; the lampstand—speaking of the glorious outshining of God in Christ, and the saints, by the Holy Spirit, answering to it; then the golden altar, figurative of the intercession of Christ. Our High Priest has charged Himself with the maintenance of the service in the holy places. Within the veil was the ark and the mercy-seat and the fragrance of the holy incense—speaking of the

presence of God, where He rests in Christ and is served by His people. We might feel unequal to all this. A brother under much pressure and in a very small locality might on occasion doubt whether he could sustain the service of God. But whatever the fewness and isolation, Christ is there to sustain us, so that we are enabled to answer to what the holy places suggest. We can count on His grace and support to maintain what is due to God in the sanctuary.
Christ is also “minister … of the true tabernacle, which the Lord has pitched, and not man”.

He maintains the whole system, extending outward, in the type, to the court and its hangings of twined byssus. Tomorrow, if the Lord will and we live, we take up our responsible paths in the world. As we appear before men we need to be maintained in a christian walk, in righteousness. For that we can count on His grace, His sympathy, His power and resource, so that everything required in testimony is maintained for God’s pleasure.

In Hebrews 12 we have the same Person spoken of as “Jesus the leader and completer of faith”. The setting is significant. Chapter 11 gives the great line of faith. Honoured Old Testament figures come before us and the chapter ends with a concentrated section including many deeds and sufferings of unnamed persons not recorded elsewhere in Scripture. It is the distinguished line of faith, all divinely noted and recorded in this roll of honour. In the verses read they are spoken of as a living “cloud of witnesses surrounding us”. Their faith encourages us, for they also were in difficult and dangerous circumstances, and they overcame. So the exhortation, is “Let us also therefore … run with endurance the race that lies before us”. In that sense we are to be worthy of those who have gone before, men and

women of faith right down to our own times, including for many of us our own parents. It is a challenge, and yet an encouragement, to lay aside “every weight, and sin which so easily entangles us”. No athlete would tolerate being weighed down. We are to discern what the weights are. Any of them would hinder us gravely. Let us discern the working of sin that so easily entangles us in the christian race. These things are to be discerned by the Holy Spirit, so that we run with endurance. And how do we run? as “looking stedfastly on Jesus the leader and completer of faith—who, in view of the joy lying before him, endured the cross, having despised the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God”.

Jesus has been through the same path as that on which we are set, facing opposition immeasurably greater than we have to face. He initiated and completed faith. He completed His pathway on that great principle, filling out as a dependent Man that life of faith. Through grace we have been called into the path. As the footnote to verse 2 shows, we are to look away from other things, fixing the eye exclusively on one, that is on Jesus. This is practical deliverance. The overcomer is one who looks steadfastly on Jesus—not like Peter when he looked at the elements and began to sink, but looking on Jesus installed in that glorious position “at the right hand of the throne of God”. Let us weigh each word of that. The whole power of Christ is for us; He said, “All power has been given me in heaven and upon earth”, Matthew 28: 18.

This chapter goes on to speak about chastening. We are not to faint under chastening, and we are to “lift up the hands that hang down, and the failing knees; and make straight paths for your feet” (Hebrews 12: 12, 13). May we be greatly encouraged and may

souls who are exercised in this country and elsewhere be strengthened to look steadfastly on Jesus so that “that which is lame be not turned aside; but that rather it may be healed”. May we thus be preserved for the glory and pleasure of God until the Lord Jesus comes, for His name’s sake.

The disciples, in dispensing the food (Luke 9), were to be representative of Christ. It is a sobering thought that in all service among the saints I am to be personally representative of Christ. What a character it would give to the service! I am not to serve because I know a thing or two, but as personally representative of Christ in His feeding activities towards His saints.
Our service would be more effective if we were more like Him—no other service is worth anything.
paragraphs.source: C. A. Coates (‘Outline of Luke’s Gospel’, p.118)

paragraphs.text: As one gets older and reviews one’s past actions one realises that they were more offensive to God than the believer judged them to be at the time of committal. As we walk with God our sense of holiness and corresponding judgment of sin increases.
